scope: Replace Highlights with Ombré across16 hairstyles, all authored worn variants and both garment-dependent twin-braid length families.
selection: Highlights is replaced by ombre/Ombré in the same preview menu position; no profile-byte assignment changes. Resolve canonical hair/hairLengths paths via catalogue253.ombre when selected. Other colors resolve the unchanged canonical252 assets. Compare252 displays its previous Highlights color, with identical geometry.
placement: Long locks retain authored root-to-tip progression. Long curls and braided sections use a continuous fall so individual braid pieces never restart the gradient. Ponytail bundles use surface-growth distance from the scalp attachment. Space-bun outer winding and raised short coils lighten progressively. Faded sides remain root-toned; Buzz is intentionally restrained. Facial hair uses the root color.
preservation: No geometry, normals, indices, alpha, transforms, silhouette, fit, body, face, clothing, skin palette or lighting changes. Primary color UV coordinates and base-color atlas are the only authored changes. Separate ties, frames/lenses and other controls remain independent.
exports: 128 ordinary, uncompressed and unquantized baked-color GLBs. Secondary UV coordinates/normal maps are preserved. ombre-gradient253.png is the shared authored color ramp. No custom renderer shader is required.
sources: Two packed reference Blender assemblies preserve fixed studio and camera settings, with embedded textures. Full authoring scripts also reference retained earlier inputs. Fair/light and Brown/dark plus skin1 have matched120/512 color/Z exports in depth253.json; camera/framing is identical across these looks.
rendering: The full Blender studio, exposure/view transform and shader graph are not carried by GLB. Ordinary PBR textures, geometry, alpha and supported material extensions transfer; native and lightweight portrait paths require their own faithful comparison.
depth: Color and32-bit float Z are generated in the same render at the same geometry/camera/version. Assembled references are not component occlusion maps or a transparent-lens solution.
qualification: Artwork color review; native renderer/portrait composition and phone workload qualification remain separate.
